references.text: David's heart 'burned' within him as he pondered – [ref:Ps 39:4|Psalm 39:4]: 'My heart grew hot within me; as I meditated, the fire burned.' This recalls the experience of the Emmaus travelers whose hearts burned within them when Jesus opened the Scriptures to them.

Jeremiah describes God's word as a burning fire in his heart – [ref:Jer 20:9|Jeremiah 20:9]: 'Then it was in my heart like a burning fire shut up in my bones.' The Emmaus travelers' 'burning heart' reflects this same experience of God's word igniting a fire within the human spirit.

The Lord's word is compared to a fire in [ref:Jer 23:29|Jeremiah 23:29]: 'Is not my word like fire, says the Lord.' The disciples experienced exactly this – Jesus' exposition of Scripture acted as fire in their hearts.

Context of the verse: In [ref:Lk 24:27|Luke 24:27] it is told that Jesus explained to them what was written about him in all the Scriptures, from Moses and all the prophets. It is this exposition of Scripture that caused the burning experience in their hearts.

Jesus opens the disciples' minds to understand the Scriptures in [ref:Lk 24:45|Luke 24:45], using a similar Greek expression (διήνοιξεν). Here he opens the Scriptures (διήνοιγεν τὰς γραφάς) for the Emmaus travelers, and later he opens the minds of all the disciples.

In [ref:Lk 24:31|Luke 24:31] the disciples' eyes were opened so that they recognized him. Verse 32 is their immediate reaction – they reflect on how they already knew him through the effect of the Word, even before their eyes were opened.

Paul's practice of expounding the Scriptures in the synagogue at Thessalonica in [ref:Acts 17:2-3|Acts 17:2-3] reflects the same pattern: opening and explaining the Scriptures to show that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead – just as Jesus did on the road to Emmaus.

In [ref:Acts 28:23|Acts 28:23] Paul expounds the Scriptures about Jesus based on the Law of Moses and the prophets, which thematically corresponds to Jesus' own exposition of Scripture on the road to Emmaus.

The prayer for eyes to be opened to God's wonderful law in [ref:Ps 119:18|Psalm 119:18] corresponds to the expression 'open the Scriptures' (διήνοιγεν τὰς γραφάς) – that God gives spiritual insight into his Word.
